description: A harvest crew needs a clean handoff between field picking, bin labeling, wash station intake, and shipment prep so traceability survives a busy multi-stage harvest day.

user_profile.persona: 40-year-old harvest supervisor coordinating several crews and downstream handling steps
user_profile.context: Speed matters during harvest, but mislabeled lots would create serious problems later in the chain
user_profile.communication_style: Operational and chain-aware, wants each handoff point made explicit

fact_sheet.fact: Marco Diaz is the Harvest Supervisor for the 2024 Sunstone peach harvest at Veridian Valley Farms.
Elena Flores leads Alpha Crew, which is assigned to harvest North Ridge Block 7.
Javier Costa leads Bravo Crew, which is assigned to harvest West Slope Block 4.
Sofia Rossi is the Wash Station Intake Manager, stationed at Wash Station A.
Each crew lead is issued a Zebra ZD421 mobile thermal printer for printing bin labels in the field.
The standard harvest container is a yellow, 250-lb capacity plastic macro bin.
Bin labels are 4x6 inch weather-resistant polyester stock, model PolyPro 4000T.
The 2024 Sunstone peach harvest began on August 15, 2024.
A bin is considered full when peaches are level with the top rim, which corresponds to an approximate weight of 250 lbs.
Full bins must be moved from the picking row to the designated block-end staging area within 15 minutes.
The crew lead is responsible for generating and applying the QR code traceability label immediately after a bin is confirmed full.
The bin label must be affixed to the north-facing side of the bin, 5 inches from the top-right corner.
Bin labels are generated using the AgriTrace Pro app on the crew's Samsung Galaxy Tab A8 tablet.
A bin's unique ID format is VV-YYMMDD-BLOCK-BIN#, for example: VV-240815-NR7-021.
Scanning a bin's QR code in the AgriTrace Pro app reveals its block of origin, crop, crew lead, and the exact timestamp of labeling.
At Wash Station A, Sofia Rossi must scan each bin's QR code before it is tipped into the hydro-cooler.
The water temperature in the hydro-cooler at Wash Station A is maintained at a constant 34°F (1.1°C).
Any bin arriving at the wash station without a scannable label is immediately moved to Quarantine Bay Q2 and flagged for 'Traceability Hold'.
The AgriTrace Pro system logs the bin's status as 'Washed' automatically upon a successful intake scan by Sofia Rossi.
Washed fruit is transported from Wash Station A to Packing Bay 3 for sorting.
To create a 'Pallet Lot' for shipment, the packing lead scans the QR codes of all bins whose fruit is packed onto that specific pallet.
The final pallet label for shipping to Golden Grocers Inc. (Purchase Order #GG-8941) must include a master QR code linking to all source bin IDs.
The web dashboard for viewing live harvest data is located at https://veridian.agritracepro.com.
The AgriTrace Pro system automatically generates an alert if the time between a bin's field scan and its wash station scan exceeds 90 minutes.
A 'Mislabeled Bin' incident report must be filed by the crew lead if a label is printed with the wrong block information, requiring a reprint and physical re-labeling within 10 minutes.
All urgent operational issues, such as a printer malfunction, must be reported in the #harvest-ops-2024 Slack channel.
For any bin placed on 'Traceability Hold', Sofia Rossi must immediately post a photo of the bin in Quarantine Bay Q2 and tag @MarcoDiaz in the Slack channel.
The mandatory end-of-day handoff meeting for all crew leads and station managers is held at 5:30 PM at the main equipment barn.
The primary contact for AgriTrace Pro software support is support@agritracepro.com, with an expected response time of 30 minutes during harvest hours.

user_needs.description: When is a harvest bin considered full in the field, and where must it be moved next?
Who is responsible for labeling a full bin and at what point in the process must this be done?
user_needs.prediction_reason: After learning the process for handling a full bin, the user's next logical question is about the labeling responsibility associated with that task.

user_needs.description: What is the exact format for a bin's unique ID, and where precisely on the bin should the label be placed?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Once the user knows who is responsible for labeling, they will need the specific instructions on what the label should contain and where it must be affixed for compliance.

user_needs.description: What is the required intake procedure for Sofia Rossi when a bin arrives at Wash Station A?
What happens if a bin arrives at the wash station without a scannable label?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After learning the standard intake procedure involves scanning a label, the immediate operational concern for a supervisor is the exception-handling process for when that scan fails.

user_needs.description: What exact Slack notification is sent to the harvest supervisor when a bin is placed on 'Traceability Hold'?
user_needs.prediction_reason: After learning that a bin can be put on hold, the supervisor's next need is to understand the communication protocol for being alerted to such an event.

user_needs.description: What is the protocol if a crew lead realizes they have printed a bin label with incorrect block information?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After understanding the correct procedure for creating and placing labels, a chain-aware supervisor would proactively consider the failure mode of an incorrect label being created in the field.

user_needs.description: Does the AgriTrace Pro system automatically generate an alert for time delays between the field scan and the wash station scan?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: Understanding the wash station intake process (the second checkpoint) naturally leads a supervisor focused on speed and efficiency to ask how the time between the first and second checkpoints is monitored.

user_needs.description: At shipment prep, how does the packing lead preserve source-bin traceability when creating a final 'Pallet Lot'?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: A supervisor with a 'chain-aware' mindset, after confirming the wash station handoff, would logically think ahead to the final step in the chain: palletizing for shipment.

user_needs.description: What is the required communication channel for reporting an urgent operational issue like a malfunctioning printer?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: Discussing the specifics of the labeling protocol and equipment naturally surfaces the critical operational question of what to do if that equipment fails.
